title: DeMIC: Decentralized Meta In-Context Learning with Refiner-Guided Adaptation

problem.claim: Inference-time in-context learning is inherently unstable, while centralized fine-tuning is infeasible when high-quality data is dispersed across private agents.

gap.claim: Existing approaches do not adequately support collaborative adaptation under privacy constraints, task heterogeneity, and dynamic network topologies.

contributions.claim: DeMIC is a decentralized meta-learning framework for collaboratively optimizing in-context adaptation under task heterogeneity and dynamic network topologies.
A Refiner-Guided mechanism constructs contrastive pairs to broaden parameter-space exploration and learn from negative samples.
The paper establishes a convergence guarantee for distributed Meta-ICL that explicitly models context-driven adaptation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe DeMIC as a novel decentralized meta-learning framework and characterize the convergence guarantee as the first for distributed Meta-ICL with explicit context-driven adaptation modeling.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant generalization to new tasks, with average improvements of 11.76% in accuracy and 10.65% in F1-score across all settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: In-context learning is presented as a promising approach for privacy-preserving distributed adaptation.
Inference-time adaptation is unstable, and centralized fine-tuning is infeasible because relevant data is private and distributed.
DeMIC addresses the setting with decentralized meta-learning and a Refiner-Guided mechanism based on contrastive pairs.
The paper states a convergence guarantee for distributed Meta-ICL with explicit context-driven adaptation modeling.
The authors report improved average accuracy and F1-score across all experimental settings.

source_observation.claim: The Refiner-Guided mechanism uses contrastive pairs and negative samples to encourage broader parameter-space exploration.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly introducing informative negative examples may reduce narrow or insufficient exploration during meta-updates.

application.claim: For distributed adaptation systems, consider contrastive refinement objectives when standard meta-updates explore too narrowly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this mechanism is effective outside the reported task, privacy, and network settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, model architectures, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not provide the convergence conditions, rate, or theorem assumptions.
The abstract does not quantify communication, computation, or privacy costs.
The abstract does not clarify how dynamic network topologies and task heterogeneity are instantiated.
